sources.title: China Three Gorges Museum: Culture of Chongqing and Yangtze
sources.content:
The Chongqing China Three Gorges Museum, formerly called the Southwest Museum (established 1951), was renamed in 2000 to focus on preserving cultural relics from the Sanxia region. It houses more than 115 thousand sets of cultural relics and 18,000 rare books across 23 categories.

Operating Information:
Hours: 9 am-5 pm daily; last entry 4:00 pm; closed Mondays
Address: No. 236 Renmin Road, Yuzhong District, Chongqing
Admission: Free with online registration required
Recommended Duration: 2-3 hours
Best Time: Year-round visits

Exhibitions (10 Permanent):
The museum features "Marvelous Three Gorges," "Ancient Ba-Yu," "Chongqing: Journey to Urbanization," "Anti-Japanese War Period," "Han Dynasty Sculpture Art," "Antique Porcelain," "Paintings and Calligraphy," "Historic Coins and Notes," "Southwest Folk Cultures," and "Collection of Li Chuli." Approximately 20-30 temporary exhibitions occur annually.

Transportation Options:
Metro: Line 2 to Zeng Jia Yan stop or Line 3 to Niu Jiao Tuo
Bus: Multiple routes (145, 152, 181, 262, 322, 338, 829, 862, 881) to nearby stops
Taxi: Readily available from city center locations
Train: Close proximity to Chongqing Railway Station

Visitor Services:
Audio guides: CNY 20 (multiple languages)
English tour guides: CNY 150-300
Luggage storage available
Bilingual signage throughout
No food/drinks permitted inside

sources.title: Essential Guide to the Three Gorges Museum: Exhibits, Tips, and Nearby Attractions
sources.content:
The Three Gorges Museum is a comprehensive historical institution in Chongqing featuring exhibits across four floors covering regional history, art, and cultural artifacts.

Hours: 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM, closed on Mondays. Last entry is at 4:30 PM.
Access: Free admission; reservations required through official WeChat.

Floor Layout:
First Floor: Magnificent Three Gorges Hall with panoramic displays of the Yangtze River and surrounding landscapes.
Second Floor (South Wing): Ancient Ba and Yu Civilization exhibition; Chongqing's urban development history.
Third Floor (North Wing): Han Dynasty sculpture artworks; Historical coins and wartime exhibits; Southwest minority cultural displays.
Fourth Floor (North Wing): Donated artifact collections (Li Chuli, Robert van Gulik family); Ancient ceramics and calligraphy exhibitions.

Notable Artifacts: Key pieces include Han Dynasty stone gates, Ming Dynasty statues, bronze drums, pottery figurines, and Tibetan Buddhist items.

Visitor Recommendations: Reserve tickets early via WeChat, wear comfortable walking shoes, bring notebooks for the museum's 46 free stamps distributed across floors, and allow a full day for exploration.

Nearby Sites: People's Great Hall (directly opposite), Zhongshan Fourth Road, Jiefangbei, and Hongyadong.

sources.title: Three Gorges Museum: Cultural Treasures & Hidden Gems in Chongqing
sources.content:
The Three Gorges Museum in Chongqing showcases treasures of the ancient Ba-Shu civilization, contemporaneous with ancient Greek culture alongside modern interpretations of Three Gorges civilization.

Location & Transportation:
Address: No. 236, Renmin Road, Yuzhong District, Chongqing
Metro: Line 1/2, Exit 3 at Zengjiayan Station (5-minute walk)
Bus: Routes 103, 122, 180 to "Three Gorges Museum" stop

Hours & Entry:
Tuesday-Sunday: 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM (last entry 4:30 PM)
Closed: Mondays (except public holidays)
Best visiting time: 9:00-10:30 AM for fewer crowds
Cost: Free regular exhibitions; special exhibitions may charge fees
Requirement: Advance WeChat reservation with ID required

Main Exhibitions:
Three Gorges Project Area (First Floor): Multimedia displays and models, including a 4D cinema featuring "Light of the Three Gorges"
Ba-Shu Culture Area (Second Floor): Bronze masks contemporaneous with the Tutankhamun mask of ancient Egypt
Hidden Gems: Folk culture exhibits, Anti-Japanese War materials, jade artistry displays, Dazu Rock Carving reproductions

Visitor Services: Audio guides in Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean. English-speaking guides (48-hour advance booking). Photography permitted (no flash).

Contact: Phone 023-63171890, Website www.3gmuseum.cn
Recommended duration: 2-3 hours minimum

sources.title: Chongqing China Three Gorges Museum: What to See & Tips
sources.content:
The Chongqing China Three Gorges Museum is a comprehensive museum of Chongqing history and art, especially those of Ba-Yu culture and Sanxia culture. Located in the heart of Chongqing, it stands as a cultural treasure that chronicles thousands of years of history in the Ba-Yu region.

Admission & Reservations: The museum is free for all visitors, but you need to make a reservation in advance on the WeChat public account. Reservations can be made 1-7 days in advance, and all visitors under 60 years old must make a reservation.

Hours: Tuesday to Sunday from 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM (last entry at 4:30 PM), closed on Mondays (except public holidays). Best time to visit: 9:00 AM to 10:30 AM.

Getting There: Take Metro Line 1/2, Exit 3 at Zengjiayan Station for a 5-minute walk.

Main Exhibits: 10 permanent exhibitions including "Marvelous Three Gorges," "Ancient Ba-Yu," "Chongqing: Journey to Urbanization," "Anti-Japanese War Period," "Han Dynasty Sculpture Art," "Antique Porcelain," "Paintings and Calligraphy," "Historic Coins and Notes," "Southwest Folk Cultures," and "Collection of Li Chuli."

Visitor Tips: Plan to spend 3-4 hours. Tourists usually visit the museum in the morning to avoid afternoon crowds.

sources.title: Three Gorges Museum (2026) - Chongqing - Tripadvisor Reviews
sources.content: Three Gorges Museum visitor reviews and ratings. The museum together with People Square and the Great Hall forms a trio of the city's landmark cultural sites. Walking from Three Gorges Museum to Chongqing People's Assembly Hall takes only 5 minutes. The museum displays four main themes covering ancient Ba-Yu culture and history, early Chongqing and the Three Gorges Dam. Most visitors spend between 1 to 2 hours exploring the main exhibits. History enthusiasts could easily spend half a day. Recommended to wear comfortable shoes as there may be long walks inside the museum.

sources.title: 重庆中国三峡博物馆_百度百科
sources.content:
重庆中国三峡博物馆（又名重庆博物馆）是首批国家一级博物馆、中央地方共建国家级博物馆，位于重庆市渝中区人民路。占地面积5万平方米，建筑面积7.17万平方米，展厅面积3.1万平方米。

历史沿革：该馆前身为1951年3月成立的西南博物院。1955年更名为重庆市博物馆，2000年9月获批改组为现名。新馆于2005年6月18日正式对外开放。

建筑布局：馆舍由五个场馆组成：主馆、重庆白鹤梁水下博物馆、重庆宋庆龄纪念馆、涂山窑遗址、重庆三峡文物科技保护中心。与人民广场、人民大礼堂形成"三位一体"的城市标志建筑群。

馆藏文物：截至2022年，馆藏文物119,772件/套，珍贵文物18,670件/套。包括旧石器、巴蜀文物、汉画像石等，涵盖23个文物门类。

重要展品：铜牵马俑（东汉）、哺乳俑（汉代）、商代三羊铜尊、战国鸟形尊、巫山猿人下颌骨化石（距今204万年）

常设展览：壮丽三峡、远古巴渝、抗战岁月、城市之路、巴蜀汉代雕塑艺术、历代瓷器、历代钱币、西南民族民俗风情等

参观信息：开放时间9:00-17:00（16:00停止入馆，周一闭馆除外），门票免费。交通：轨道2号线曾家岩站、3号线牛角沱站、10号线大礼堂站。

荣誉：2008年晋升国家一级博物馆，2020年当选巴蜀文化旅游走廊新地标，2023年入选全国热搜博物馆百强。2024年1-8月接待游客234万人次。

sources.title: 重庆三峡博物馆游玩攻略 - 携程攻略
sources.content:
重庆三峡博物馆游玩攻略。博物馆共分四层，主要由360度环幕电影、4个基本陈列（《壮丽三峡》、《远古巴渝》、《重庆·城市之路》、《抗战岁月》）和6个专题陈列等组成。

推荐游玩路线：三峡博物馆→重庆市人民大礼堂→中山四路→李子坝单轨穿楼→鹅岭二厂→鹅岭公园

建议游玩时间：3-4小时

门票：对公众实行免票开放，采取实名制网上预约、分时接待、错时分批入馆等举措。可提前1-7天预约，通过微信公众号或小程序进行预约。

馆藏文物11.5万余件套（单件超28万件），珍贵古籍善本1.8万余册，涵盖23个文物门类。
